workload.problem: damped harmonic oscillator x'' + 2 zeta omega x' + omega^2 x = 0, classical RK4, fixed step (perf_card.py)

arm_labels.eagle_term8: eagle host, termination loop, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_compact8: eagle host, termination + compaction, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_reorder8: eagle host, termination + compaction + reorder, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_reorder1: eagle host, termination + compaction + reorder, 1 thread

arms.eagle_term8: The GPU card's eagle graph arm, unchanged, on the host: the same hawk step kernel, eagle.deploy and eagle.until_done call, run by eagle's OpenMP host team; one code base for GPUs and CPUs. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 17.9 ms; spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 162 ms; uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 123 ms. Fastest in 12 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_term1: The same loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 129 ms (7.23× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.27 s (7.84× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 915 ms (7.44× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_compact8: The GPU card's compaction arm on the host: the launch covers only the samples still running, the map rebuilt every 16 steps when a sample finished. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 57.9 ms (3.24× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 321 ms (1.98× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 885 ms (7.19× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_compact1: The compaction loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 191 ms (10.7× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.37 s (8.44× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.77 s (30.7× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_reorder8: The GPU card's reorder arm on the host: the live samples moved to the front of every plane when they spread thin, restored to sample order at the end (inside the wall). On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 127 ms (7.12× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 362 ms (2.24× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 919 ms (7.47× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_reorder1: The reorder loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 232 ms (13× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 933 ms (5.76× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.78 s (30.8× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.numba_prange: Compiles a plain Python loop to machine code with no separate language; each sample keeps its state in registers across all of its steps and stops on its own, so finished samples cost nothing. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 34.6 ms (1.94× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 335 ms (2.07× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.59 s (13× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.jax_shard8: The JAX arm spread over 8 CPU devices: the batch is sharded and each shard runs its own vmapped while loop, with no cross-shard step synchronisation. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 108 ms (6.02× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.03 s (6.35× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.03 s (8.34× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.jax_vmap: Compiles the whole loop once and batches a per-sample while loop with vmap; the same code runs on GPUs and differentiates with jax.grad. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 244 ms (13.7× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.55 s (15.7× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.4 s (19.5× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.torch_masked: Runs the masked array version on a multi-threaded tensor library; it fits where the computation already lives next to a PyTorch model or needs autograd. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 790 ms (44.2× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 7.39 s (45.6× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 7.24 s (58.9× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.numpy_masked: No compile step and no dependency beyond NumPy; masked array code computes every sample every step, so it fits dense batches where all samples run to the end (the uniform configuration). On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 3.23 s (181× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 29.1 s (180× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 28.4 s (231× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.mp_numpy: Spreads NumPy over processes with the standard library alone; each chunk stops once its own samples are done. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 431 ms (24.1× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.69 s (22.8× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.6 s (29.3× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.python_loops: Nothing to install and each line can be stepped in a debugger; run only at small N here. On this card: spread S=100, N=10,000: 39.5 ms (186× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=10,000: 372 ms (197× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000: 169 ms (1.03e+03× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
